Main observations:

- `price 15-100, drop fallback` is the cleanest drawdown reducer by year:
  - improves 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 yearly DD versus base;
  - also improves 2020 DD versus base;
  - but the total return is weak (`$33.630k`, CAGR 7.9%, Sharpe 0.378).
- `ret60 <= -20%, drop fallback` is the strongest return repair but not a drawdown repair:
  - improves 2020 P&L strongly;
  - worsens yearly DD in 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024 versus base.
- `ret60 <= -20%, price 15-100, drop fallback` is the best balance among tested filters:
  - improves yearly DD in 2021, 2023, and 2024;
  - 2020 DD remains high (`-$20.996k`) though better than base;
  - 2022 DD is still slightly worse than base (`-$15.779k` vs `-$14.703k`);
  - total stats: `$50.182k`, CAGR 10.8%, DD `-$24.761k`, Sharpe 0.528.
- Dropping yday is not enough:
  - it helps 2020/2023/2024 DD;
  - but it makes 2021 and 2022 yearly DD worse, and overall DD remains very high.

Sleeve/year attribution:

- Base yday is the main drag in 2020, 2021, 2023, and the August/September 2024 drawdown.
- In 2022, broad/local are the main problem; yday often helps. This is why filters that reduce yday
  cannot fully fix 2022 and can even make 2022 worse.
- `ret60 <= -20%, price 15-100, drop fallback` removes most yday damage in 2023/2024 and turns 2021
  yday positive, but 2022 remains a broad/local regime issue.

Verdict:

- There is no filter here that both restores high return and reliably reduces drawdown by year.
- Best DD filter: `price 15-100, drop fallback`, but return is too weak.
- Best balanced filter: `ret60 <= -20%, price 15-100, drop fallback`, but still only modest return and
  still has 2020/2022 risk.
- Next cheap check should focus on 2020 crash and 2022 broad/local drawdown, not on further yday
  micro-filtering.

### 6.135 Market-regime overlay for 2020/2022 broad-local drawdown

Question:

> 2022 losses line up with market selloff periods. Can a simple market-regime overlay reduce broad/local
> drawdown without destroying the edge?

Script:

- `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_regime_overlay_nowarmup.py`

Outputs:

- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_REGIME_OVERLAY_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_SUMMARY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_REGIME_OVERLAY_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_YEARLY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_REGIME_OVERLAY_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_2022_MONTHLY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_REGIME_OVERLAY_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_REGIME_DAILY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_REGIME_OVERLAY_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_SIGNAL_QA.csv`

Regime inputs:

- `spy20`: 20-session compounded `spy_prev_dayret` proxy from the broad feature cache.
- `univ20`: 20-session compounded equal-weight broad-universe previous-day return.
- `breadth20`: 20-session average percent of broad-universe names positive on previous-day return.

The overlay is causal with respect to the current open because it uses previous-session returns. The
test skips new broad/local entries on risk-off days and leaves yday unchanged. This is a coarse
entry filter, not a dynamic de-risking of already-open positions.

2022 market context:

- Base 2022 max DD period: 2022-03-29 to 2022-06-16.
- During that period:
  - strategy PnL: `-$12.735k`;
  - SPY proxy: `-10.3%`;
  - broad-universe equal-weight proxy: `-12.1%`;
  - average positive breadth: 46.0%.
- The worst base months were April (`-$7.431k`), June (`-$4.789k`), December (`-$3.353k`), and
  September (`-$2.495k`).

Balanced yday variant tested:

`ret60 <= -20%, price 15-100, drop fallback`

Summary:

| overlay | PnL | CAGR | DD | Sharpe | avgGross | note |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| none | `$50.182k` | 10.8% | `-$24.761k` | 0.528 | 0.730x | baseline balanced |
| skip broad+local if `univ20 < -8%` | `$42.588k` | 9.5% | `-$19.490k` | 0.520 | 0.702x | best risk/return trade-off |
| skip broad only if `univ20 < -8%` | `$46.787k` | 10.3% | `-$22.773k` | 0.522 | 0.718x | keeps more return, weaker DD cut |
| skip local only if `univ20 < -8%` | `$46.007k` | 10.1% | `-$20.568k` | 0.531 | 0.714x | best specific-sleeve compromise |
| skip broad+local if `spy20 < -5%` | `$41.319k` | 9.3% | `-$20.281k` | 0.509 | 0.688x | similar |
| skip broad+local if any risk-off trigger | `$29.579k` | 7.1% | `-$18.772k` | 0.416 | 0.647x | too defensive |
| skip broad only if any risk-off | `$41.385k` | 9.3% | `-$22.002k` | 0.485 | 0.693x | less useful |
| skip local only if any risk-off | `$37.572k` | 8.6% | `-$19.405k` | 0.477 | 0.684x | return haircut too high |

Yearly PnL/DD for selected overlays on the balanced yday variant:

| year | no overlay PnL / DD | `univ20 < -8%` PnL / DD | any risk-off PnL / DD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2018 | `-$2.238k` / `-$9.019k` | `-$2.648k` / `-$8.853k` | `-$2.242k` / `-$8.219k` |
| 2019 | `$8.360k` / `-$5.828k` | `$6.843k` / `-$5.639k` | `$6.517k` / `-$5.713k` |
| 2020 | `$10.342k` / `-$20.996k` | `$5.259k` / `-$19.490k` | `$0.811k` / `-$18.772k` |
| 2021 | `$10.435k` / `-$12.331k` | `$9.538k` / `-$10.778k` | `$8.610k` / `-$10.210k` |
| 2022 | `-$7.368k` / `-$15.779k` | `-$4.439k` / `-$12.591k` | `-$4.442k` / `-$11.722k` |
| 2023 | `$15.046k` / `-$11.004k` | `$13.600k` / `-$10.216k` | `$9.165k` / `-$9.750k` |
| 2024 | `$15.607k` / `-$6.485k` | `$14.436k` / `-$5.994k` | `$11.161k` / `-$5.216k` |

Interpretation:

- Yes, a market-regime overlay reduces 2022 drawdown.
- It also reduces drawdown in most other years.
- But it is a return haircut. The broad/local sleeves make a lot of their money during volatile
  periods, especially 2020, so broad risk-off filters cut both pain and edge.
- The broad-universe trend trigger (`univ20 < -8%`) is the cleanest tested compromise: DD improves by
  about `$5.3k` versus no overlay, while CAGR falls from 10.8% to 9.5%.
- Applying that trigger to a specific sleeve is better than expected. Skipping only local on
  `univ20 < -8%` keeps more return than skipping both broad and local (`$46.007k` vs `$42.588k`) while
  still cutting DD materially (`-$20.568k` vs `-$24.761k` baseline). Skipping only broad keeps slightly
  more P&L (`$46.787k`) but DD is worse (`-$22.773k`).
- The any-risk-off trigger is too blunt: DD improves, but PnL collapses back near base.

Verdict:

- Market regime explains a meaningful part of 2022 drawdown, but not enough to create a strong
  candidate.
- Best risk-control hypothesis so far:
  - yday: `ret60 <= -20%, price 15-100`;
  - exclude `liquidity_metric_source == ticker_fallback`;
  - either skip local only when broad-universe 20-session return `univ20 < -8%`, or skip both
    broad+local if the priority is lower DD.
- Specific-sleeve result: `$46.007k`, CAGR 10.1%, DD `-$20.568k`, Sharpe 0.531.
- Broader risk-off result: `$42.588k`, CAGR 9.5%, DD `-$19.490k`, Sharpe 0.520.
- This is safer but still not attractive enough for production. Treat it as a diagnostic risk-control
  variant, not a promotion.

### 6.136 Restricted-62 broad PIT replay and rank-displacement audit

User asked why the Polygon-62 tickers do not produce the same 2023-2024 trade result once the broad
PIT universe is used. I ran a direct universe-competition check: take the broad PIT feature cache,
restrict it to the exact tickers traded by `B_polygon62_no_intraday_cap40_PIT`, rebuild broad/local/yday,
apply the same PIT gate, and replay the same B no-intraday engine.

Scripts:

- `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_restricted62_nowarmup.py`
- `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_restricted62_rank_displacement_nowarmup.py`

Outputs:

- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_RESTRICTED62_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_SUMMARY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_RESTRICTED62_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_COMPARE_TO_POLY62_FROM_START.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_RESTRICTED62_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_TRADE_KEY_OVERLAP.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_RESTRICTED62_RANK_DISPLACEMENT_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_SUMMARY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_RESTRICTED62_RANK_DISPLACEMENT_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_DETAIL.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_RESTRICTED62_RANK_DISPLACEMENT_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_REPLACEMENTS.csv`

Restricted-62 broad PIT replay:

| run | period | PnL | CAGR | DD | Sharpe | trades | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| full broad PIT nowarmup B | 2018-03-29..2024-12-31 | `$29.361k` | 7.1% | `-$23.691k` | 0.271 | 46,102 | `$3.303k` | `$15.734k` |
| restricted-to-62 PIT nowarmup B | 2018-03-29..2024-12-31 | `$91.363k` | 16.6% | `-$13.834k` | 1.141 | 31,324 | `$26.095k` | `$22.868k` |
| Polygon-62 PIT warmup B | 2018-01-02..2024-12-31 | `$107.082k` | 17.8% | `-$14.216k` | 1.193 | 31,569 | `$29.063k` | `$27.880k` |

This answers the main question: the low full-broad result is not primarily because PIT 5m data or the
engine cannot reproduce the Polygon-62 behavior. When the same broad PIT data is restricted to the old
62 tickers, the result comes back close to the Polygon-62 lead. The main loss is universe competition:
the full broad universe adds many more eligible names, and the old 62 picks are displaced by the ranking
rules.

2023-2024 sleeve comparison, restricted PIT versus Polygon-62 warmup from the restricted start window:

| sleeve | restricted PIT 2023 | Polygon-62 2023 | restricted PIT 2024 | Polygon-62 2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| broad | `$7.859k` | `$9.075k` | `$5.751k` | `$9.460k` |
| local | `$9.984k` | `$10.797k` | `$8.569k` | `$9.418k` |
| yday | `$5.335k` | `$5.749k` | `$7.997k` | `$8.755k` |

Rank displacement:

- Broad: in the full PIT universe, many restricted-62 broad picks are no longer top-20 by 5-day selloff
  strength. Over 2018-2024, only 1,216 of 14,607 restricted-62 broad picks rank 1-20 in the full
  candidate list; 10,807 rank 51-500. In 2023-2024, 3,238 of 4,283 restricted-62 broad picks rank
  51-500. Even top-20 candidates are not always selected because the broad sleeve also has active ticker
  caps and existing positions.
- Local: displacement is more direct because local is simple top-10 cross-sectional ranking. Over
  2018-2024, only 116 of 16,590 restricted-62 local picks remain rank 1-10 in the full universe. In
  2023-2024, only 26 of 4,780 remain top-10. Most are ranked 101-500 in the full universe.
- Yday: the WFO path changes almost completely. Rolling3 restricted-62 yday has 127 picks over
  2018-2024, but only 1 overlaps the full broad PIT yday picks; in 2023-2024 overlap is zero.

Interpretation:

- The broad PIT replay is not "same strategy, same 62 winners, plus extra fill." It is a different
  selection problem. The original 62-stock universe was implicitly a strong quality/liquidity/mega-cap
  filter; broad PIT removes that filter and lets many lower-quality or more extreme names take the
  top ranks.
- Restricted-62 PIT recovering `$91.363k` versus full broad PIT `$29.361k` is strong evidence that the
  performance gap is mainly universe selection/competition, not a fatal PIT data join bug.
- However, restricted-62 is still not a valid production answer because it inherits the old
  survivor/curated-universe concern. It is a diagnostic that explains the failure mode.

Verdict:

- The current broad PIT family remains WARN/research-only.
- The next useful test should not be more micro-filtering of yday. It should define a causal quality
  universe or pre-registered quality gate that can make the broad universe resemble a tradable quality
  stock universe without hindsight-selecting the 62 winners.

### 6.137 Causal quality-universe gates on broad PIT

Following 6.136, I tested whether simple causal quality gates can make the full PIT universe behave more
like the implicit Polygon-62 quality/mega-cap universe. These gates use only information available before
entry:

- prior close;
- PIT trailing ADV20;
- prior 20-day volatility;
- no `ticker_fallback` liquidity rows;
- optional daily top-N by trailing ADV20.

Script:

- `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_quality_universe_gate_nowarmup.py`

Outputs:

- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_QUALITY_UNIVERSE_GATE_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_SUMMARY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_QUALITY_UNIVERSE_GATE_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_YEARLY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_QUALITY_UNIVERSE_GATE_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_SIGNAL_QA.csv`

Implementation note: the gate is applied after rolling features are computed, but before each sleeve's
selection/ranking. This preserves refill semantics. For broad, non-quality rows remain available for
mark-to-market pricing, but are removed from the candidate list by blanking their `ret5` signal. For
yday, the daily signal table is gated before WFO rule selection, so the WFO can choose/refill from the
quality universe rather than merely deleting trades after selection.

Summary, B no-intraday nowarmup:

| variant | PnL | CAGR | DD | Sharpe | trades | quality tickers | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| price >= 10, ADV >= 50m, no fallback | `$20.102k` | 5.1% | `-$23.787k` | 0.219 | 48,728 | 2,121 | `$6.574k` | `$9.467k` |

- Threshold gates are too loose: even after price/ADV/no-fallback filters, the universe still has
  roughly 1,500-2,100 tickers over the test window, so the old 62-style names are still heavily diluted.
- Top-N ADV is closer to a causal quality universe, but it exposes a new problem: 2022 selloff damage

- The implicit Polygon-62 filter likely contained more than liquidity: stable large-cap/quality names,

Verdict:

- Causal price/ADV/volatility quality gates: FAIL as a recovery path.
- Top200 ADV gate: weak diagnostic improvement, not a candidate.
- Broad PIT family remains WARN/research-only. The next defensible direction would need either:
  - a true historical large-cap/index-membership/market-cap universe, or
  - a pre-registered quality model trained only before the test window and audited for 2022 risk.

### 6.138 Reverse-profile quality gates from the Polygon-62 universe

User correctly challenged 6.137: if the old 62-stock universe implicitly represented large-cap /
quality / index-like names, we should apply that profile back to the full PIT universe rather than only
using blunt price/ADV thresholds. I added reverse-profile diagnostics to the same script.

Script:

- `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_quality_universe_gate_nowarmup.py`

Outputs:

- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_QUALITY_UNIVERSE_GATE_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_SUMMARY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_QUALITY_UNIVERSE_GATE_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_YEARLY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_QUALITY_UNIVERSE_GATE_NOWARMUP_2026-09-13_SIGNAL_QA.csv`

Available local PIT metadata still has no sector or market cap. So the reverse profile uses causal
proxies:

- daily percentile rank of PIT ADV20;
- daily percentile rank of prior close;
- daily percentile rank of prior 20-day volatility;
- history age/coverage;
- no `ticker_fallback` liquidity rows.

The profile is trained from Polygon-62 tickers during 2018-2020, then applied to the full PIT universe.
This is **not** a production-ready candidate because it learns from the old 62-stock universe, but it is
a much better diagnostic of what the missing universe filter is doing.

Reverse-profile variants:

- `profile62_train_q10`: keep names inside the loose q10/q90 profile envelope learned from 62.
- `profile62_train_q25`: keep names inside the stricter q25/q75 profile envelope learned from 62.
- `profile62_score_top100`: each day, keep the 100 names closest to the learned 62-profile centroid.
- `profile62_score_top200`: each day, keep the 200 names closest to the learned 62-profile centroid.

Interpretation:

  materially improves results versus both the full PIT base and the simple ADV/price gates.
- The improvement is not just liquidity. `top200 ADV only` had worse DD and only `$33.825k`; the
  profile variants reach `$45k-$55k` with much better Sharpe/DD.
- The best diagnostic is `profile62_score_top100`: PnL `$55.055k`, CAGR 11.6%, DD `-$11.184k`, Sharpe

- This strongly suggests the old universe had an implicit "large, seasoned, reasonably priced,
  moderate-volatility" filter, not just a current-survivor list.

Verdict:

- Reverse-profile filter: PASS as a diagnostic, WARN as a candidate hypothesis.
- Do not promote it yet because it was learned from the old 62 universe and still lacks real sector,
  index-membership and market-cap history.
- Next defensible step: freeze `profile62_score_top100` as a hypothesis, then either:
  - replace the proxy profile with true historical large-cap/index/market-cap data; or
  - run a nested protocol where the quality profile is learned only from pre-test years and evaluated
    forward year by year.

### 6.139 Why profile62 still does not recover the 2023-2024 Polygon-62 result

User asked why, if the reverse-profile quality gate works, the 2023-2024 result still does not recover
the old Polygon-62 tickers. I audited `profile62_score_top100` against the restricted-62 picks.

Script:

- `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_profile62_selection_audit_nowarmup.py`

Outputs:

- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_PROFILE62_SELECTION_AUDIT_NOWARMUP_2026-09-14_SUMMARY.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_PROFILE62_SELECTION_AUDIT_NOWARMUP_2026-09-14_DETAIL.csv`
- `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_PROFILE62_SELECTION_AUDIT_NOWARMUP_2026-09-14_REPLACEMENTS.csv`

Key 2023-2024 findings:

- Local is mostly fixed by the profile gate:
  - 1,535 restricted-62 local picks are rank 1-10 inside the profile universe and all 1,535 are selected.
  - These overlap trades contribute `$5.937k`.
  - The profile replacements add only `$4.398k`, with lower avg PnL (`$1.36` vs `$3.87`).
- Broad is only partly fixed:
  - 2,566 restricted-62 broad picks are allowed by the profile universe in 2023-2024.
  - Only 479 broad picks overlap the profile-selected broad candidate file.
  - Even restricted-62 names ranked 1-10 in the profile universe are selected only 74/354 times.
  - Reason: the broad sleeve is not a simple top-N snapshot; it has 20-day holding, active ticker caps,
    active positions and gross/capacity constraints. A ticker can be high-ranked today but not selected
    if it is already active or capacity/ticker-cap blocks it.
- Yday is still the main "does not recover 62" problem:
  - 69 restricted-62 rolling3 yday picks in 2023-2024.
  - Only 6 overlap the profile-selected yday picks.
  - Those 6 overlap trades contribute `$4.756k`, all winners.
  - The 13 profile yday replacements lose `-$2.124k`.
  - This means the profile gate improves the universe but does not force WFO to choose the same yday
    rule/ticker path as Polygon-62.

Compact answer:

- The profile gate gets the universe closer, but it does not exactly recreate the 62-stock selection
  process.
- It recovers local well, partially recovers broad, and barely recovers yday.
- 2023-2024 remains lower because the missing PnL is concentrated in the exact old yday/broad winners,
  especially yday. The profile filter lets similar names in, but replacements are weaker.

Verdict:

- `profile62_score_top100` is a valid diagnostic improvement, not a full recovery.
- The next hardening should focus on yday rule-selection under the profile universe and broad active
  position/cap interaction, not more simple universe thresholds.

Narrowing the universe does not recreate the path. Top50 improves 2023 but gives up 2024 and still
stays far below restricted-62.

Yday rule-path audit:

Restricted-62 inferred rolling3 yday rules:

| year | restricted-62 rule |
|---:|---|
| 2020 | `raw_-6` |
| 2021 | `raw_-7` |
| 2022 | `quality_-5_gapdown_mompos` |
| 2023 | `gapdown_-4` |
| 2024 | `gapdown_-4` |

Profile WFO chooses different rules, often raw panic rules. Freezing yday to the restricted-62 rule
path helps materially but does not fully recover the old picks.

Standalone yday, selected examples:

| variant | path | yday PnL | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `profile62_score_top100` | WFO | `$24.672k` | `$0.113k` | `$2.519k` |
| `profile62_score_top100` | frozen restricted rules | `$26.397k` | `$10.714k` | `$2.578k` |
| `profile62_train_q25` | WFO | `$12.546k` | `-$1.144k` | `$2.158k` |
| `profile62_train_q25` | frozen restricted rules | `$20.413k` | `$4.475k` | `$3.741k` |

Full engine with frozen yday restricted rules:

| variant | PnL | CAGR | DD | Sharpe | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `profile62_score_top100` + frozen yday rules | `$57.114k` | 11.9% | `-$11.907k` | 0.935 | `$14.756k` | `$9.629k` |
| `profile62_train_q25` + frozen yday rules | `$59.118k` | 12.2% | `-$13.854k` | 1.041 | `$14.487k` | `$14.361k` |
| restricted-to-62 PIT diagnostic | `$91.363k` | 16.6% | `-$13.834k` | 1.141 | `$26.095k` | `$22.868k` |

Interpretation:

- Yes, there is a partial way to recreate the path: reverse-profile universe plus frozen yday rule path.
- But it still does not recreate the exact 62-stock path. The full-engine result improves from
  `$55.055k` to `$57.114k` for top100, or to `$59.118k` for the q25 profile, but remains far below
  restricted-62.
- The missing piece is not only rule selection. It is exact membership / ranking / active-position path:
  the profile universe admits "similar" names, but not the same exact winners. For 2023-2024, replacing
  even a small number of old yday/broad winners changes PnL a lot.

Answer:

- To recreate the **exact** path, one of these must be true:
  - use the actual 62-ticker universe as the universe definition, which is not production-valid unless
    that universe can be justified causally; or
  - use true historical membership data that caused the 62-like names to be eligible at the time:
    historical large-cap index membership, market cap ranking, sector/index constraints, or another
    externally-defined universe.
- With only local proxy fields (ADV, price, volatility, age), we can approximate but not exactly recreate
  the old selection path.

Verdict:

- Recreate-exact with current local proxy data: FAIL.
- Recreate-partial with profile + frozen yday rules: PASS as diagnostic, still WARN as candidate.
- The next real step is external/historical universe data, or treat the 62-ticker universe itself as a
  manually-defined product universe and stop calling it broad survivorship-safe PIT.

### 6.142 Decision checkpoint: not a money printer yet

This section is the current status checkpoint for the whole Polygon-62 / broad-PIT universe thread.
If returning later, start here, then read 6.136-6.141 for details.

Question being answered:

Can the current stock strategy be called a "money printer", or is it only a research lead whose apparent
edge depends on the 62-stock universe?

Current answer:

**Not a money printer yet.** The strategy is a research lead / diagnostic family, not production-ready.

State of the main branches:

| branch | result | verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| Full broad PIT nowarmup B | `$29.361k`, CAGR 7.1%, DD `-$23.691k`, Sharpe 0.271 | FAIL / research-only |
| Restricted-to-62 PIT nowarmup B | `$91.363k`, CAGR 16.6%, DD `-$13.834k`, Sharpe 1.141 | strong diagnostic, but universe/curation WARN |
| Polygon-62 PIT warmup B | `$107.082k`, CAGR 17.8%, DD `-$14.216k`, Sharpe 1.193 | old lead, still WARN+ |
| Reverse-profile `profile62_score_top100` | `$55.055k`, CAGR 11.6%, DD `-$11.184k`, Sharpe 0.860 | diagnostic improvement, not enough |
| Reverse-profile + frozen yday rules, q25 | `$59.118k`, CAGR 12.2%, DD `-$13.854k`, Sharpe 1.041 | partial path recovery, still WARN |

Important interpretation:

- The old 62-stock universe is a huge part of the result.
- Full broad PIT does not reproduce the edge.
- Simple price/ADV/volatility filters fail.
- Reverse-profile filters prove the user was directionally right: the old 62-stock universe acted like a
  quality/large-cap/index-like filter. But proxy profile fields do not fully recreate the old selection
  path.
- Exact restricted-62 path is traceable, but not recreatable from current local proxy fields without
  either using the 62 tickers directly or getting true historical large-cap/index/market-cap/sector data.
- 2023-2024 missing PnL is mostly exact yday/broad winners. Local is mostly recovered by profile; yday is
  the main unrecovered blocker.

Benchmark sanity:

- The restricted-62 branch has attractive Sharpe/DD, but its raw 2023-2024 return is not obviously better
  than a simple bull-market buy-and-hold benchmark after considering complexity, turnover, data risk and
  universe concerns.
- Therefore the correct label is **research lead survives, not standalone money printer**.

Recommended next action:

1. Stop micro-optimizing this branch with more price/ADV/vol thresholds.
2. If continuing this branch, do exactly one high-quality validation:
   - build/acquire true historical large-cap/index/market-cap/sector membership;
   - rerun the strategy on that pre-defined historical universe;
   - compare against SPY/QQQ and equal-weight large-cap buy-and-hold on return, drawdown and Sharpe.
3. If that fails, close this branch and open a new edge search.

Do not promote:

- `restricted62` as production unless the 62-name universe is explicitly defined as a manual product
  universe and the survivorship/curation risk is accepted.
- `profile62_*` as production; it was learned from the old 62 universe and is diagnostic only.

### 6.145 Polygon-62 universe provenance trace

User asked whether the 62 tickers can be traced to an exact rule such as top sector/top market cap.
I traced the artifact chain backwards from the current Polygon-62 caches.

Chain:

```text
stocks_polygon_fetch_5min_2018_2024_62.py
  reads tickers from stocks_intraday_0935_features_CAUSEQA_2026-09-10.pkl
stocks_feature_cache_builder.py
  built that cache from window_debug_5min.pkl
window_debug_5min.pkl
  was built by raits/raits/scripts/window_debug.py from its static TICKERS list
```

The exact source in `raits/raits/scripts/window_debug.py` is:

```text
TICKERS = ["SPY", "QQQ", "IWM"] + SECTOR_ETFS + UNIVERSE + PHASE1 + PHASE2 + PE_EXPANSION
```

I verified this exact set against `raits/data/cache/window_debug_5min.pkl`:

- computed tickers from `window_debug.py`: 75
- unique computed tickers: 75
- actual tickers in `window_debug_5min.pkl`: 75
- missing in actual: none
- extra in actual: none
- equities after removing SPY/QQQ/IWM and sector ETFs: 62

Exact 62-equity breakdown:

| bucket | count | tickers |
|---|---:|---|
| Original fixed universe | 8 | TSLA, NVDA, AAPL, META, AMZN, MSFT, AMD, GOOGL |
| Phase 1 new stocks | 20 | INTU, COST, VRTX, AMAT, REGN, AVGO, ADBE, MS, SBUX, TXN, XOM, AMGN, ORCL, EBAY, QCOM, CVX, CSCO, GS, CRM, JPM |
| Phase 2 new stocks | 9 | MU, HON, MA, NFLX, INTC, V, GILD, BIIB, MMM |
| PE_SHORT expansion | 25 | PFE, MRK, LLY, ABBV, JNJ, BMY, BAC, WFC, C, WMT, TGT, HD, LOW, MCD, NKE, PG, KO, PEP, CAT, DE, BA, GE, PYPL, PANW, NOW |

Non-equity/ETF additions in the old raw cache:

- Index ETFs: SPY, QQQ, IWM
- Sector/other ETFs: XLF, XLE, XLV, XLU, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLB, XLY, GLD

Interpretation:

- The 62 tickers are **not** generated by a clean live rule such as top market cap, top sector,
  S&P 500 membership, or Nasdaq-100 membership.
- They are a staged/static research universe:
  - original 8 mega-cap/growth names;
  - 20 Phase 1 names, documented in-code as "downloaded 2019-2022, >=248 scanner-audit days";
  - 9 Phase 2 names, documented in-code as "downloaded after Phase 1 results confirmed";
  - 25 PE_SHORT expansion names.
- This is stronger provenance than the earlier "current survivor 62" label, but it is also a
  stronger overfit/curation warning: Phase 1 and Phase 2 were explicitly added after prior results
  or scanner audits, and PE expansion was strategy-specific.

Verdict:

- Exact origin rule: traced.
- Production-safe live universe rule: **not traced**.
- Correct label: **staged/manual research universe**, not objective market-cap/index/sector universe.
- Any production candidate using this universe must either:
  1. explicitly accept it as a manual product universe; or
  2. replace it with a pre-declared live rule and re-run the strategy.

### 6.146 Pre-registered broad-PIT new edge search: overnight/09:35 XS diagnostic

After the 62-name provenance trace, I stopped trying to recreate the old 62 universe and started a clean
new edge search on broad PIT data. This first pass is diagnostic only, with the candidate family fixed
before running.

Pre-registered hypothesis families for the new search:

1. Cross-sectional overnight / first-5min reversal or continuation on broad PIT names.
2. Gap/event-like behavior using only PIT-safe event proxies; external earnings labels are excluded until
   PIT-safe provenance is proven.
3. Large-cap/top-market-cap universe with sector-balanced slots, pre-registered before replay.
4. Regime-conditioned broad/local signals with fixed entry-time regimes.
5. Benchmarks against SPY/QQQ/equal-weight/top-market-cap universes.

| gap tail 1%, rvol2 reversal L/S | HIG | 0.6% | 1.5% | 2.1% | 3.3% | 507.0 |

Interpretation:

- This is worse than "costs killed a tiny edge": every variant is negative **before** costs.
- Extreme gapdown long reversal is especially weak in 2020-2021, and only intermittently positive in
  2019/2022.
- Extreme gapup short/fade has positive 2018 and 2021, but loses badly in 2019, 2020 and 2022-2024.
- Concentration is not the problem; top-10 positive ticker share stays low and effective ticker count is
  broad.

Verdict:

- `gap_event_safe` as implemented here: **KILL**.
- No production PASS, no robust candidate, and no needs-audit promotion.
- Do not tune gap thresholds or rvol thresholds from this result. If continuing gap/event research, the
  next pass must introduce a genuinely new pre-registered dimension, such as PIT-safe sector/industry
  context or an independently defined earnings/event label, rather than squeezing these gap/rvol knobs.

- Full broad PIT no-intraday B from 6.142: `$29.361k`, DD `-$23.691k`, Sharpe 0.271.

Interpretation:

- Simple beta/large-cap exposure is a high absolute-return hurdle in 2018-2024.
- The old restricted-62 strategy still looks much better on drawdown-normalized quality, but it is not
  obviously better on raw dollars versus simple market-cap top62 equal-weight or SPY.
- Broad PIT signal families that produce `$30k-$55k` with non-trivial data/turnover complexity are weak
  unless they offer materially better drawdown or portfolio diversification.
- Top-market-cap equal-weight is materially concentrated: top10 contribution is 45.6% for top62 and 32.8%
  for top100. This must not be mistaken for a diversified edge.
- Broad equal-weight is diversified but has very large 2020 and 2022 drawdowns.

Verdict:

- Benchmark hurdle: **continue as context**, not a production PASS.
- This raises the bar for new alpha: future candidates need to beat either:
  1. SPY/top-market-cap beta on risk-adjusted and drawdown-normalized terms; or
  2. broad PIT equal-weight on diversification/hedging value.
- Next honest dig, if continuing, should be a pre-registered sector/SIC-balanced top-market-cap diagnostic:
  keep market-cap exposure, cap sector/industry dominance, then measure whether drawdown/concentration
  improves without relying on the old 62 names.

### 6.150 Market-cap beta risk-control diagnostic

Important sample label:

The recent broad-PIT diagnostics use the available 2018-2024 PIT research window, generally from
2018-03-29 through 2024-12-31 after feature availability. This is **not clean unseen OOS**. In particular,
2023-2024 has already been touched by prior research and must be treated as touched validation / regime
context only. The only reason to keep using 2018-2024 here is that 2025-2026 remains unopened by instruction,
and the current task is broad-PIT edge search, not production validation.

After 6.149 showed that SIC bucket caps do not solve the market-cap benchmark drawdown/concentration issue,
I ran a fixed causal risk-control diagnostic on top of the benchmark daily return streams.

Question:

Can a simple causal exposure overlay keep the useful market-cap beta while reducing drawdown enough to become
a worthwhile benchmark/risk-control clue?

Data contract / leakage controls:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_mcap_beta_risk_control.py`
- Input:
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BENCHMARK_HURDLES_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
- Outputs:
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_MCAP_BETA_RISK_CONTROL_2026-09-14_SUMMARY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_MCAP_BETA_RISK_CONTROL_2026-09-14_YEARLY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_MCAP_BETA_RISK_CONTROL_2026-09-14_SPLITS.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_MCAP_BETA_RISK_CONTROL_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_MCAP_BETA_RISK_CONTROL_2026-09-14_MANIFEST.json`
- Base streams: `market_cap_top62_equal_weight` and `market_cap_top100_equal_weight` from 6.148.
- Exposure is causal:
  - vol target uses trailing 20-day realized benchmark volatility shifted by one day;
  - trailing-loss rule uses trailing 20-day compounded return shifted by one day.
- No old-62 equity list or reverse-profile filter is used beyond the benchmark provenance already documented
  in 6.148.
- Rule-selection effect: none. Four variants were fixed before measuring.
- OOS caveat: all rows are research diagnostics; `2023_2024_touched` is not clean OOS.

Pre-registered variants:

- `top62_voltarget_12pct_cap100`: target 12% annualized vol, max exposure 100%.
- `top100_voltarget_12pct_cap100`: target 12% annualized vol, max exposure 100%.
- `top62_trail20_loss8_half`: if trailing 20-session return <= -8%, cut exposure to 50%.
- `top100_trail20_loss8_half`: if trailing 20-session return <= -8%, cut exposure to 50%.

| top100 voltarget 12% | `$78.288k` | 8.9% | `-$28.469k` | -17.8% | 0.735 | 0.816x | 53.4% |
| top62 trail20 loss8 half | `$117.296k` | 12.2% | `-$56.205k` | -28.6% | 0.741 | 0.983x | 3.4% |
| top100 trail20 loss8 half | `$105.154k` | 11.2% | `-$49.511k` | -26.9% | 0.686 | 0.981x | 3.8% |

Reference rows:

| reference | PnL | CAGR | dollar DD | pct DD | Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| plain market-cap top62 EW | `$132.916k` | 13.3% | `-$52.205k` | -32.3% | 0.746 |
| plain market-cap top100 EW | `$108.257k` | 11.5% | `-$46.588k` | -33.7% | 0.651 |
| SPY buy-and-hold | `$125.527k` | 12.8% | `-$46.648k` | -34.2% | 0.700 |
| restricted-to-62 PIT nowarmup B | `$91.363k` | 16.6% | `-$13.834k` | not reported there | 1.141 |

Yearly PnL:

| variant | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| top62 voltarget 12% | `$4.533k` | `$21.782k` | `$18.030k` | `$27.015k` | `-$23.428k` | `$21.118k` | `$28.387k` |
| top100 voltarget 12% | `$1.245k` | `$19.094k` | `$14.080k` | `$22.948k` | `-$19.384k` | `$20.115k` | `$20.190k` |
| top62 trail20 loss8 half | `-$0.420k` | `$26.214k` | `$31.934k` | `$37.788k` | `-$42.488k` | `$28.705k` | `$35.564k` |
| top100 trail20 loss8 half | `-$4.083k` | `$24.728k` | `$27.153k` | `$35.083k` | `-$33.450k` | `$28.473k` | `$27.249k` |

Chronological split view:

| variant | 2018-2021 research | 2022 stress | 2023-2024 touched |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| top62 voltarget 12% | `$71.360k`, DD `-$18.281k`, Sharpe 1.261 | `-$23.428k`, DD `-$30.452k`, Sharpe -1.189 | `$49.505k`, DD `-$17.506k`, Sharpe 1.337 |
| top100 voltarget 12% | `$57.366k`, DD `-$17.976k`, Sharpe 1.069 | `-$19.384k`, DD `-$26.745k`, Sharpe -1.065 | `$40.305k`, DD `-$16.303k`, Sharpe 1.183 |
| top62 trail20 loss8 half | `$95.516k`, DD `-$32.098k`, Sharpe 1.225 | `-$42.488k`, DD `-$56.205k`, Sharpe -1.236 | `$64.269k`, DD `-$18.563k`, Sharpe 1.515 |
| top100 trail20 loss8 half | `$82.882k`, DD `-$30.891k`, Sharpe 1.105 | `-$33.450k`, DD `-$49.511k`, Sharpe -1.001 | `$55.722k`, DD `-$18.321k`, Sharpe 1.347 |

Interpretation:

- Vol targeting is the first broad-PIT follow-up that improves the benchmark risk profile in a meaningful
  way without using old-62 selection:
  - top62 DD improves from `-$52.205k` to `-$30.452k`;
  - top62 pct DD improves from -32.3% to -17.7%;
  - top62 Sharpe improves from 0.746 to 0.853.
- The improvement is not free: top62 PnL drops from `$132.916k` to `$97.437k`.
- The trailing 20-day loss rule is too blunt/late: it keeps nearly full exposure most of the time and does
  not improve DD enough.
- 2022 remains the stress problem even under vol targeting, but the loss/DD is reduced materially versus
  plain top-market-cap exposure.
- This is beta/risk-control evidence, not alpha evidence. It should be compared honestly against SPY and
  simple market-cap benchmarks, not treated as a stock-selection edge.

Verdict:

- `top62_voltarget_12pct_cap100`: **continue / needs audit** as a benchmark/risk-control clue.
- `top100_voltarget_12pct_cap100`: **context only**; lower return and lower Sharpe than top62 voltarget.
- `trail20_loss8_half` variants: **kill**; not enough DD improvement.
- No production PASS. The next clean step would be to pre-register a small beta/risk-control family, add
  transaction/cash feasibility assumptions, and reserve any truly unseen future period before promotion.

Verdict:

- Do not tune top-N/lookback/pool from this result.
- Only reasonable follow-up is a causal risk-control overlay on the already-fixed momentum rows, to test
  whether the raw momentum clue can be made less dangerous.

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_vol_state_allocator.py`

- This is another beta risk-shaping result, not a new alpha stream.
- Because this is a return-stream allocator, it does not add new ticker concentration evidence. Any future

- Volatility-state allocator: **KILL / no stop condition met**.
- Do not tune more realized-vol thresholds from these results.

Interpretation:

- Narrowing to large caps and adding simple trend/vol filters does not rescue intraday gap/first-5-minute
  signals.
- Gross PnL is weak or negative; after realistic round-trip cost, every row is deeply negative.
- Concentration is broad, so the failure is not a single-name issue. The signal family itself is weak.
- This reinforces the earlier broad-universe intraday kill rather than creating a new candidate.

Verdict:

- Large-cap 09:35 intraday selection: **KILL / no stop condition met**.
- Do not tune intraday rank tails, gap thresholds, or first-5-minute filters from these results.

  vol-targeted SPY sleeve. That makes financing, short borrow, margin, and execution assumptions first-order.

  so far because it nearly reaches the return target after a constituent-level refill/cost audit.

Verdict:

- `SPY vt16 + top62/top200 spread x3`: **CONTINUE / NEEDS AUDIT**, not production PASS.
- Next audit should test whether the same structure survives realistic short borrow/financing, lower gross
  caps, and a pre-registered stress guard without using 2023-2024 or old-62 information as clean OOS.

- This confirms the audit concern from 6.171: leverage/financing assumptions are first-order, not cosmetic.

Verdict:

- 5x-gross `SPY vt16 + top62/top200 spread x3`: **KILL for production / keep as diagnostic clue**.
- Continue search, but do not pursue high-gross long/short spread overlays unless financing, borrow,
  concentration, and margin constraints are built into the objective from the start.

### 6.173 Finance-aware low-gross mega-cap spread scan

After section 6.172 killed the 5x-gross candidate, I tested whether the same market-cap top62/top200
spread can help at lower gross when financing and borrow are included from the start.

Data contract / leakage controls:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_beta_plus_megaspread_lowgross_scan.py`
- Input:
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_PLUS_MEGASPREAD_AUDIT_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
- Outputs:

  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_PLUS_MEGASPREAD_LOWGROSS_SCAN_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_PLUS_MEGASPREAD_LOWGROSS_SCAN_2026-09-14_MANIFEST.json`
- Sample: inherits 2018-03-29 through 2024-12-31 from section 6.171. 2023-2024 is touched; 2025-2026
  remains unopened.
- Method: fixed rescaling of the audited SPY vt16 sleeve and constituent top62/top200 spread. Tested
  SPY scales 0.75/1.00/1.25 and spread weights 0.50/1.00/1.50.
- Costs: keeps the section 6.171 spread turnover cost, then adds 2.5% annual financing on gross exposure
  above 1x and 1.0% annual borrow on estimated short gross.
- Rule-selection effect: none inside this diagnostic. The 9-row grid was fixed before running.
- Trade-selection effect: inherited from section 6.171 constituent refill.

Summary:

| variant | CAGR | PnL | dollar DD | pct DD | Sharpe | avg gross exp |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SPY 0.75 + spread 0.50 | 11.4% | `$107.080k` | `-$29.439k` | -16.6% | 0.860 | 1.53x |
| SPY 1.00 + spread 0.50 | 14.4% | `$148.074k` | `-$44.411k` | -21.6% | 0.801 | 1.81x |
| SPY 1.25 + spread 0.50 | 17.3% | `$193.852k` | `-$62.561k` | -26.5% | 0.753 | 2.09x |
| SPY 0.75 + spread 1.00 | 10.6% | `$97.236k` | `-$32.930k` | -18.5% | 0.771 | 2.22x |
| SPY 1.00 + spread 1.00 | 13.6% | `$136.251k` | `-$48.218k` | -23.4% | 0.739 | 2.50x |
| SPY 1.25 + spread 1.00 | 16.4% | `$179.827k` | `-$66.642k` | -28.1% | 0.706 | 2.78x |
| SPY 0.75 + spread 1.50 | 9.7% | `$87.330k` | `-$36.533k` | -20.5% | 0.671 | 2.91x |
| SPY 1.00 + spread 1.50 | 12.7% | `$124.396k` | `-$51.926k` | -25.2% | 0.669 | 3.19x |
| SPY 1.25 + spread 1.50 | 15.6% | `$165.797k` | `-$70.636k` | -29.8% | 0.654 | 3.47x |

Interpretation:

- Lower gross plus realistic carry cost removes the 25% CAGR profile. The best CAGR is 17.3%, and it comes
  with -26.5% DD.
- The lower-DD row, SPY 0.75 + spread 0.50, has -16.6% DD but only 11.4% CAGR.
- Increasing spread weight worsens the tradeoff after financing/borrow because the spread's standalone
  return is too small relative to its gross exposure.
- This confirms that the section 6.170/6.171 clue was mostly useful as a low-correlation component, not as
  a finance-aware production engine.

Verdict:

- Finance-aware low-gross mega-cap spread: **KILL for 25% CAGR target**.
- Do not continue tuning this spread family without a new ex-ante reason; further leverage/ratio tweaks
  would be optimization around a touched sample.

### 6.174 Cost-aware long-only beta governor

I tested a separate, fixed long-only beta governor family after killing the high-gross spread branch. The
question was whether lagged crash/volatility rules can support higher target volatility while keeping DD
lower, without long/short financing dependency.

Data contract / leakage controls:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_beta_governor_costaware.py`
- Input:
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BENCHMARK_HURDLES_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
- Outputs:
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_GOVERNOR_COSTAWARE_2026-09-14_SUMMARY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_GOVERNOR_COSTAWARE_2026-09-14_YEARLY.csv`

  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_GOVERNOR_COSTAWARE_2026-09-14_MANIFEST.json`
- Sample: 2018-2024 research/touched sample only. 2023-2024 is not clean unseen OOS; 2025-2026 remains
  unopened.
- Universe: fixed `market_cap_top62_equal_weight` and `spy_buy_hold` benchmark streams from section 6.148.
- Method: target-vol exposure using lagged 20-day realized vol; risk-off when lagged 20-day return is below
  -8% or -5%, or lagged 20-day vol is above 25% or 30%, depending on fixed row.
- Costs: 2.5% annual financing on exposure above 1x, plus 4 bps per dollar of exposure turnover.
- Rule-selection effect: none inside this diagnostic. Twelve rows were fixed before running.
- Trade-selection effect: inherited from the PIT benchmark streams; this is not a ticker removal/refill test.

Summary:

| variant | CAGR | PnL | dollar DD | pct DD | Sharpe | avg exposure | risk-off days |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| top62 vt20 cap200 riskoff50 ret20 -8 vol20 25 | 14.2% | `$145.942k` | `-$72.127k` | -32.4% | 0.635 | 1.47x | 10.8% |
| top62 vt25 cap250 riskoff50 ret20 -8 vol20 25 | 15.9% | `$170.718k` | `-$101.698k` | -40.3% | 0.565 | 1.82x | 10.8% |
| top62 vt25 cap200 riskoff50 ret20 -8 vol20 25 | 15.2% | `$160.922k` | `-$95.969k` | -39.3% | 0.603 | 1.62x | 10.8% |
| top62 vt25 cap250 riskoff50 ret20 -5 vol20 25 | 16.2% | `$175.613k` | `-$97.551k` | -38.9% | 0.585 | 1.79x | 14.2% |
| top62 vt25 cap250 riskoff50 ret20 -8 vol20 30 | 16.8% | `$186.461k` | `-$108.539k` | -40.9% | 0.584 | 1.84x | 5.1% |
| SPY vt20 cap200 riskoff50 ret20 -8 vol20 25 | 14.3% | `$147.261k` | `-$51.768k` | -26.5% | 0.668 | 1.41x | 13.1% |
| SPY vt25 cap250 riskoff50 ret20 -8 vol20 25 | 16.2% | `$176.693k` | `-$71.243k` | -33.2% | 0.612 | 1.75x | 13.1% |
| SPY vt25 cap200 riskoff50 ret20 -8 vol20 25 | 16.6% | `$181.994k` | `-$69.807k` | -32.5% | 0.687 | 1.58x | 13.1% |

Interpretation:

- The governor does not solve the target. Best CAGR is 16.8% for top62 and 16.6% for SPY, both far below
  25%.
- DD remains poor relative to the return. The best SPY row still has -32.5% DD, while top62 rows are around
  -32% to -41%.
- The lagged guard is too late for 2022. For example, `SPY vt25 cap200 riskoff50` still loses `-$65.347k`
  in 2022 with `-$69.807k` subset DD.
- The audit lesson about dollar and pct DD matters here: some lower-return rows reduce dollar DD only
  because the account curve is smaller; pct DD does not confirm a robust improvement.

Verdict:

- Cost-aware long-only beta governor: **KILL for 25% CAGR / low-DD target**.
- Do not keep tuning ret20/vol20 thresholds on this touched sample without a fresh pre-registered reason.

### 6.175 Cost-aware turn-of-month calendar timing

I tested a separate ex-ante calendar family: turn-of-month / first-days liquidity timing on fixed SPY,
market-cap top62, and market-cap top100 benchmark streams. This avoids ticker picking and old-62

Data contract / leakage controls:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_turn_of_month_costaware.py`

Summary:

| variant | CAGR | PnL | dollar DD | pct DD | Sharpe | active days |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| SPY last2+first3 x2.5 | 14.3% | `$147.035k` | `-$79.621k` | -24.7% | 0.494 | 23.9% |
| SPY first5 x2.5 | 19.1% | `$225.217k` | `-$87.541k` | -23.5% | 0.665 | 23.9% |
| top62 last1+first3 x3.0 | 5.2% | `$40.933k` | `-$57.159k` | -29.6% | 0.175 | 19.3% |

Interpretation:

- There is a positive calendar timing signal, especially first5 trading days, but it is not strong enough

  2024; SPY last2+first3 loses `-$58.020k` in 2024.
- This family is useful as benchmark context but not a robust standalone edge.

Verdict:

### 6.177 Lagged equity drawdown circuit breaker

After the calendar overlay still showed unacceptable losses, I tested a drawdown-budget-first circuit
breaker on the strongest prior beta/calendar streams and two raw beta streams. The goal was to see whether
losses can be kept plausibly tolerable without destroying the edge.

Data contract / leakage controls:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_equity_dd_circuit_breaker.py`
- Inputs:
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_PLUS_CALENDAR_OVERLAY_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_VOLTARGET_EXPANSION_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
- Outputs:
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_EQUITY_DD_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_2026-09-14_SUMMARY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_EQUITY_DD_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_2026-09-14_YEARLY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_EQUITY_DD_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_EQUITY_DD_CIRCUIT_BREAKER_2026-09-14_MANIFEST.json`
- Sample: 2018-2024 research/touched sample only. 2023-2024 is not clean unseen OOS; 2025-2026 remains
  unopened.
- Method: each day's scale is based only on prior close strategy equity drawdown. Tested fixed DD cuts
  -10%/-15%, risk-off scale 0.25, and recovery at -4%/-6%.
- Costs: 4 bps per dollar of scale turnover.
- Rule-selection effect: none. Source streams and DD thresholds were fixed before running.
- Trade-selection effect: none beyond inherited prior streams.

Summary:

| source / breaker | CAGR | PnL | dollar DD | pct DD | Sharpe | risk-off days | avg scale |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SPY vt20 + SPY first5, DD10 | 6.5% | `$52.955k` | `-$21.007k` | -15.2% | 0.472 | 83.9% | 0.37 |
| SPY vt20 + SPY first5, DD15 | 5.9% | `$46.878k` | `-$32.558k` | -18.8% | 0.384 | 78.6% | 0.41 |
| SPY vt16 + SPY first5, DD10 | 5.9% | `$47.754k` | `-$23.200k` | -14.8% | 0.502 | 80.5% | 0.40 |
| SPY vt16 + top62 first5, DD10 | 11.1% | `$103.191k` | `-$30.308k` | -14.5% | 0.832 | 72.7% | 0.45 |
| top62 vt25, DD10 | 8.2% | `$69.976k` | `-$29.019k` | -15.8% | 0.516 | 75.0% | 0.44 |
| SPY vt20, DD10 | 3.8% | `$28.958k` | `-$21.378k` | -14.8% | 0.323 | 80.5% | 0.40 |

Interpretation:

- The circuit breaker can cap full-period DD into the -15% to -20% zone, but only by keeping the book
  risk-off for roughly 73%-84% of trading days.
- CAGR falls to 4%-11%, far below the target. This is risk suppression, not a surviving 25% edge.
- The best tradeoff row is `SPY vt16 + top62 first5, DD10`: 11.1% CAGR, -14.5% DD, Sharpe 0.83. That is
  investable-looking risk control context, but not the requested edge.
- This also confirms that a simple trailing equity stop would not have saved the high-return rows without
  giving up most upside.

Verdict:

- Lagged equity DD circuit breaker: **KILL for 25% CAGR / low-DD target**.
- Useful risk-control diagnostic, but not a path to the requested profile by itself.

### 6.178 Monthly loss limiter

I tested a softer risk-control rule than section 6.177: reset the loss budget every month and scale down
only after prior-close month-to-date loss breaches a fixed threshold.

Data contract / leakage controls:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_monthly_loss_limiter.py`
- Inputs:
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_PLUS_CALENDAR_OVERLAY_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_BETA_VOLTARGET_EXPANSION_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
- Outputs:
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_MONTHLY_LOSS_LIMITER_2026-09-14_SUMMARY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_MONTHLY_LOSS_LIMITER_2026-09-14_YEARLY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_MONTHLY_LOSS_LIMITER_2026-09-14_DAILY.csv`
  - `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_MONTHLY_LOSS_LIMITER_2026-09-14_MANIFEST.json`
- Sample: 2018-2024 research/touched sample only. 2023-2024 is not clean unseen OOS; 2025-2026 remains
  unopened.
- Method: if prior close month-to-date strategy equity return is below -5% or -8%, scale to 0.25 until the
  next calendar month.
- Costs: 4 bps per dollar of scale turnover.
- Rule-selection effect: none. Source streams and monthly thresholds were fixed before running.
- Trade-selection effect: none beyond inherited prior streams.

Summary:

| source / limiter | CAGR | PnL | dollar DD | pct DD | Sharpe | risk-off days |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SPY vt20 + SPY first5, MTD -5 | 19.6% | `$234.426k` | `-$105.626k` | -34.2% | 0.670 | 18.3% |
| SPY vt20 + SPY first5, MTD -8 | 19.9% | `$240.766k` | `-$98.674k` | -31.3% | 0.642 | 10.0% |
| SPY vt16 + SPY first5, MTD -8 | 18.8% | `$221.224k` | `-$77.175k` | -26.0% | 0.714 | 7.2% |
| SPY vt16 + top62 first5, MTD -8 | 19.0% | `$224.701k` | `-$83.902k` | -26.9% | 0.711 | 7.2% |
| top62 vt25, MTD -5 | 20.4% | `$251.010k` | `-$89.783k` | -30.6% | 0.726 | 16.2% |
| SPY vt20, MTD -5 | 15.8% | `$169.010k` | `-$48.475k` | -23.4% | 0.734 | 12.7% |

Interpretation:

- Monthly reset avoids the permanent risk-off problem from section 6.177, but it does not create a low-DD
  high-return profile.
- The high-return rows still have unacceptable losses: `SPY vt20 + SPY first5` remains around -31% to -34%
  DD after the limiter.
- The lower-DD `SPY vt20, MTD -5` row has -23.4% DD but only 15.8% CAGR.
- The limiter is often too late: it reacts after the month has already taken damage, then can miss the
  rebound. This is why some rows have worse DD than the unfiltered source.

Verdict:

- Monthly loss limiter: **KILL for 25% CAGR / low-DD target**.
- Risk-control overlays alone are not enough; the next search should favor genuinely lower-drawdown alpha,
  not post-loss throttling.

- The calendar-conditioned relative spread is negative after realistic financing/borrow/turnover costs.
- The active long/short spread is only a few bps per active day, so costs dominate.
- Scaling to 2x simply doubles the problem and worsens DD.

Verdict:

- Calendar-conditioned mega-cap relative spread: **KILL**.
- Do not combine the spread with calendar windows further without a new reason; both components have already
  been audited and costs are first-order.

### 6.180 Top500 gap multi-day rebound / continuation

I tested a gap/event-like family without earnings labels: use the same-day opening gap as the signal, enter
at the same day's close, then hold an overlapping long-only book for multiple days. This avoids using event
labels that may not be PIT-safe and reduces turnover versus daily gap scans.

Verdict:

- Top500 gap multi-day rebound/continuation: **KILL for 25% CAGR / low-DD target**.

walk-forward ridge ranker over PIT top500 stocks, predicting next 5-day close-to-close return and

  top100 loses `-$63.771k`.
- Long/short rows reduce DD but produce negative return after costs and borrow.
- Model coefficients are unstable by year; signs on short-horizon reversal/trend features change across
  training windows, which is not a robust edge signature.

Interpretation:

- The current feature set does not support a profitable weekly ML ranker. The long side mostly recreates
  unstable beta/high-vol exposure, and the long/short side cannot cover cost/borrow.
- Concentration is not the main issue for top100; effective ticker count is 216.3. The issue is weak
  predictive edge and poor stress behavior.
- This is a useful negative result because it tests a stricter WFO engine instead of another in-sample
  variant tweak.

Verdict:

- Walk-forward weekly ML ranker on current PIT features: **KILL for 25% CAGR / low-DD target**.
- A production ML direction would need richer PIT-safe features or event data, not more tuning of this
  simple feature set.

### 6.186 Walk-forward 09:35 weekly ranker

This diagnostic tests a genuinely different holding-period use of the 09:35 cache. Section 6.167 entered
at 09:35 and exited at 15:55 every day, so weak gross edge was overwhelmed by daily round-trip costs.
Here the signal is measured at 09:35 but positions are held until the next weekly 09:35 rebalance.

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_wfo_0935_weekly_ranker.py`
- Inputs:
  - `raits/data/cache/stocks_clean_daily_features_PIT_FULL_2018_2024_NOWARMUP.pkl`

  - `raits/data/cache/external_universes/market_cap_polygon/polygon_market_cap_snapshots_pit_eligible_2018_2024.csv`
- Output prefix: `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_WFO_0935_WEEKLY_RANKER_2026-09-17_*`
- Research sample: features begin 2018-03-29; frozen yearly walk-forward tests cover 2019-2024.
  The entire period is touched research data. 2023-2024 is not clean unseen OOS and 2025-2026 remains
  unopened.
- Universe: quarterly PIT market-cap top500, assigned backward from the latest available snapshot. The old
  manual/restricted 62 universe is not used.
- Features known by 09:35 only: cross-sectionally winsorized/z-scored gap, first-five-minute return,
  log relative 09:30 volume, lagged 20/60-day return, lagged 20-day volatility, gap x first-five-minute,
  open-to-09:35 return, and absolute gap.
- Target: return from the current weekly 09:35 price to the next global weekly rebalance's 09:35 price.
- Walk-forward: each test-year ridge model trains only on earlier years. Boundary rows are purged unless
  their label end date is strictly before the test-year cutoff.
- Costs: 4 bps per unit of target-weight turnover; long/short variants also pay 1.0% annual borrow on short
  gross.
- Rule-selection effect: none inside this diagnostic. The feature set, interactions, ridge alpha, target,
  weekly schedule and four portfolio variants were fixed before measuring.
- Trade-selection effect: every weekly membership set and rank is rebuilt from PIT inputs and the frozen
  model for that year. There is no ticker-PnL subtraction or post-selection refill shortcut.

For the low-net-PnL long/short rows, shares above 100% mean the largest winners are offset by losses in

four rows, but the long rows still have broad effective ticker counts.

Predictive and audit read:

- Mean weekly rank IC is small in every test year: 1.9%, 2.6%, 1.3%, 0.2%, 0.2%, and 2.6% from 2019
  through 2024. It is essentially absent in the 2022 stress and 2023 touched windows.
- The long portfolios mostly retain market beta. Their positive full-period PnL does not survive the 2022
  stress, and dollar and equity-normalized DD are both unacceptable.
- Neutralizing the book exposes the weak standalone alpha: long/short CAGR is only 1.5%-1.8% after cost
  and borrow.
- A constituent-accounting audit changed held-name pricing from the selected top500 panel to the broad PIT
  panel, so a name leaving a quarterly snapshot remains marked until rebalance. The result was directionally
  unchanged. Some held names still lack a valid 09:35 bar on isolated dates (maximum 25 positions on one
  day), so missing-bar treatment remains a limitation, not a reason to promote the result.

Verdict:

- Walk-forward 09:35 weekly ranker: **KILL for the 25% CAGR / low-DD target**.
- Do not tune rank cutoffs, ridge alpha, feature subsets or leverage on 2018-2024. The current local cache
  does not show enough 09:35 cross-sectional alpha to support that search.
- The next defensible edge search needs a new PIT-safe information source, such as timestamped earnings /
  corporate-event data or richer order-flow/auction features, with a new pre-registered family. Recombining
  the existing daily, gap, first-five-minute, beta and calendar features is now heavily exhausted.
- Useful clue for risk reduction, but not a production-grade edge.

### 6.187 PIT top500 09:35 confirmed/rejected event-shock cohorts

After the WFO 09:35 model showed only weak standalone alpha, I ran one fixed rule-based diagnostic to
separate two economically distinct opening events: a large overnight gap confirmed by the first five
minutes, and a large gap rejected by the first five minutes. This is not an earnings study because no
PIT-safe earnings labels are available in the local inputs.

Data contract / leakage controls:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_0935_event_shock_cohorts.py`
- Inputs:
  - `raits/data/cache/stocks_clean_daily_features_PIT_FULL_2018_2024_NOWARMUP.pkl`
  - `raits/data/cache/stocks_intraday_0935_features_PIT_FULL_2018_2024_NOWARMUP.pkl`
  - `raits/data/cache/external_universes/market_cap_polygon/polygon_market_cap_snapshots_pit_eligible_2018_2024.csv`
- Outputs use prefix `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_0935_EVENT_SHOCK_COHORTS_2026-09-17_` and include summary,
  yearly, concentration, daily, ticker contribution, selected signals, QA, and manifest files.
- Sample: 2018-03-29 through 2024-12-31, research/touched only. 2023-2024 is not clean unseen OOS;
  2025-2026 remains unopened.
- Universe: PIT quarterly market-cap top500, assigned backward to each signal date. Held names are marked
  from the broad PIT price panel even after a snapshot change.
- Base event: absolute overnight gap at least 2% and 09:30 relative volume at least 1.5.
- Confirmed event: first-five-minute move at least 0.25%, same sign as the gap; trade the 09:35 direction.
- Rejected event: first-five-minute move at least 0.50%, opposite sign to the gap; trade the rejection
  direction.
- Portfolio: one 20%-gross cohort per day, held for exactly five trading sessions. Long/short cohorts use
  at most five names per side; long-only cohorts use at most ten positive names. Structural max gross is 1x.
- Costs: 4 bps aggregate target-weight turnover and 1.0% annual borrow on short gross.
- Rule-selection effect: none. Thresholds, ranking, hold period, cohort gross and all four variants were
  fixed before measuring.
- Trade-selection effect: candidates and overlapping cohorts are rebuilt daily from PIT inputs; no
  ticker-PnL subtraction or post-period ticker selection. Old manual 62 is not used.

Summary:

| variant | CAGR | PnL | dollar DD | pct DD | Sharpe | avg / max gross | signals |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| confirmed gap long/short | 1.8% | `$12.730k` | `-$18.143k` | -16.7% | 0.158 | 0.71x / 1.00x | 6,654 |
| rejected gap long/short | -4.2% | `-$24.725k` | `-$42.304k` | -37.9% | -0.401 | 0.66x / 1.00x | 5,429 |
| confirmed gap long | 10.0% | `$89.367k` | `-$40.483k` | -22.3% | 0.416 | 0.74x / 1.00x | 4,070 |
| rejected gap long | 2.0% | `$13.796k` | `-$61.004k` | -50.3% | 0.102 | 0.67x / 1.00x | 3,073 |

Yearly PnL for the two confirmed-gap rows:

| variant | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| confirmed gap long/short | `$3.212k` | `-$9.832k` | `$6.084k` | `$11.408k` | `-$3.374k` | `$8.270k` | `-$3.039k` |
| confirmed gap long | `$5.951k` | `$10.259k` | `$24.240k` | `$30.897k` | `-$19.212k` | `$24.117k` | `$13.115k` |

Concentration:

| variant | effective tickers | top1 share | top3 share | top5 share | top10 share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| confirmed gap long/short | 78.1 | 83.9% | 206.0% | 314.9% | 476.4% |
| rejected gap long/short | 141.6 | 1.1% | 3.1% | 4.8% | 7.9% |
| confirmed gap long | 83.7 | 21.7% | 52.3% | 73.1% | 113.5% |
| rejected gap long | 132.6 | 59.8% | 145.1% | 202.0% | 331.5% |

Shares above 100% mean the largest winners are offset by losses elsewhere. The best-return row is therefore
not broad-based: its top ten winners exceed total net PnL. Missing held-name 09:35 bars are limited but not
zero (maximum three positions on one day), and are retained as an audit limitation.

Interpretation:

- Confirmation is directionally better than rejection, but market-neutral confirmation earns only 1.8%
  CAGR after cost and borrow. That is the cleanest read of standalone cross-sectional alpha.
- The 10.0% CAGR confirmed long row mainly adds market beta and still loses `$19.212k` in 2022. It misses
  the 25% CAGR target and its concentration is too high to call robust.
- Rejected-gap behavior is unstable: the long/short row is negative and the long row has -50.3% DD.
- This fixed multi-day implementation avoids the daily round-trip cost problem from 6.167, but the edge
  remains too weak. Scaling it would scale concentration and drawdown, not create a low-DD 25% profile.

Verdict:

- PIT top500 09:35 event-shock cohorts: **KILL for the 25% CAGR / low-DD target**.
- Do not tune the gap, rvol, first-five-minute thresholds, hold period or rank count on this touched sample.
- Continue only with a genuinely new PIT-safe information source, preferably timestamped earnings/corporate
  events or richer opening-auction/order-flow fields. The current local daily plus 09:35 feature set is
  exhausted for this target.

### 6.188 PIT top500 residual-reversal cohorts

This diagnostic tests the remaining distinct price-only hypothesis: temporary idiosyncratic price pressure.
Unlike the raw prior-day reversal in 6.162, the signal removes either the daily broad-universe move or the
same-day SIC-group move before ranking. It also enters at 09:35 on the next trading day and uses overlapping
multi-day cohorts to reduce churn.

Data contract / leakage controls:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_residual_reversal_cohorts.py`
- Inputs:
  - `raits/data/cache/stocks_clean_daily_features_PIT_FULL_2018_2024_NOWARMUP.pkl`
  - `raits/data/cache/stocks_intraday_0935_features_PIT_FULL_2018_2024_NOWARMUP.pkl`

- Outputs use prefix `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_RESIDUAL_REVERSAL_COHORTS_2026-09-17_` and include summary,

- Sample: 2018-03-29 through 2024-12-31, research/touched only. 2023-2024 is not clean unseen OOS;
  2025-2026 remains unopened.
- Universe: quarterly PIT market-cap top500 with backward snapshot assignment. SIC labels come from the
  same PIT-eligible Polygon snapshots. The old manual/restricted 62 universe is not used.
- Market residual: completed prior-session stock return minus the same-date PIT top500 median; long the ten
  lowest residuals and short the ten highest.
- SIC residual: completed prior-session stock return minus the same-date SIC median; in buckets with at
  least eight names, long one residual loser and short one residual winner.
- Entry: next trading session at 09:35. Fixed overlapping cohorts hold three or five sessions. Each cohort
  has gross `1 / holdDays`, so structural aggregate gross is at most 1x.
- Costs: 4 bps aggregate target-weight turnover and 1.0% annual borrow on short gross.
- Rule-selection effect: none. Residual definitions, tails/pairs, next-day entry, hold3/hold5 family, gross,
  and costs were fixed before measuring.
- Trade-selection effect: daily constituents and every overlapping cohort are rebuilt from PIT inputs.
  There is no ticker-PnL subtraction, removal shortcut, or post-period ticker selection.

| market residual, hold5 | `-$3.059k` | `$1.702k` | `$3.273k` | `$1.134k` | `$16.860k` | `-$5.206k` | `-$2.437k` |
| SIC residual, hold3 | `-$4.411k` | `-$4.127k` | `$3.936k` | `-$1.514k` | `$3.472k` | `-$2.528k` | `-$0.400k` |

Concentration:

| variant | effective tickers | top1 share | top3 share | top5 share | top10 share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

| market residual, hold5 | 134.7 | 37.5% | 76.0% | 108.5% | 169.7% |
| SIC residual, hold3 | 61.0 | 2.4% | 6.5% | 9.4% | 14.5% |

For the negative SIC rows, concentration shares use absolute PnL as the denominator. For the positive market
rows, shares above 100% show that losses outside the largest winners offset much of their contribution.

Interpretation:

- Market-residual reversal has positive gross PnL, but 64%-70% is consumed by turnover and borrow. Net
  CAGR is only 1.7%-2.2%, with 19%-22% drawdown.
- The apparent edge is not stable. Most full-period market-residual profit comes from 2022; hold5 is negative
  in both 2023 and 2024, while hold3 is approximately flat in those touched years.
- Removing SIC-group movement eliminates the net edge. Both SIC-neutral rows are negative after costs,
  suggesting that part of the market-residual result is industry reversal rather than stock-specific alpha.
- Concentration also fails the robustness test: the top five market-residual winners exceed total net PnL.
- Held names are priced from the broad PIT 09:35 panel, not only the selected top500 panel. Missing 09:35
  bars remain limited but non-zero, with a maximum of eight held positions on one day; this is an audit
  limitation and cannot rescue the weak result.

Verdict:

- PIT top500 residual-reversal cohorts: **KILL for the 25% CAGR / low-DD target**.
- Do not tune residual tails, SIC bucket size, hold duration, costs, or leverage on the touched 2018-2024
  sample. The only positive form is small, year-unstable, cost-heavy, and winner-dependent.
- The locally available price/volume feature families are now exhausted at a useful first-pass level. A
  defensible next search requires genuinely new PIT-safe event or microstructure data, not another
  recombination of the same daily and 09:35 fields.

### 6.189 Rolling PIT same-SIC pairs diagnostic

One price-only family remained structurally different from cross-sectional ranking: rolling same-industry
pairs. This diagnostic forms pairs only from trailing data, freezes every pair and hedge parameter until the
next scheduled formation, observes spread z-score at the close, and trades at 09:35 next session.

Data contract / leakage controls:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_rolling_sic_pairs.py`
- Inputs:
  - `raits/data/cache/stocks_clean_daily_features_PIT_FULL_2018_2024_NOWARMUP.pkl`
  - `raits/data/cache/stocks_intraday_0935_features_PIT_FULL_2018_2024_NOWARMUP.pkl`
  - `raits/data/cache/external_universes/market_cap_polygon/polygon_market_cap_snapshots_pit_eligible_2018_2024.csv`
- Outputs use prefix `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_ROLLING_SIC_PAIRS_2026-09-17_`. Formation parameters, daily
  signals, trade events, constituent contributions, QA, and the manifest are persisted in addition to the
  summary/yearly/daily outputs.
- Sample: 2018-03-29 through 2024-12-31, research/touched only. A formation requires 120 local sessions,
  so the quarterly row has no 2018 trades. 2023-2024 is not clean unseen OOS; 2025-2026 remains unopened.
- Universe: quarterly PIT market-cap top500 and PIT-eligible Polygon SIC label. Old manual 62 is not used.
- Formation: trailing 120 sessions, at least 100 paired observations, return correlation at least 0.60,
  no ticker reuse, and at most two pairs per SIC. Pairs are re-formed monthly or quarterly.
- Frozen spread: trailing return regression beta, applied to log-price spread; formation mean/std stay
  frozen until the next formation.
- Trading: enter when absolute z-score is at least 2.0, exit on absolute z-score at most 0.5, sign crossing,
  formation removal, or fixed 5/10-session timeout. Signals observed at close execute next session at 09:35.
- Portfolio: at most ten active pairs, equal pair gross, dollar-neutral pair legs, max gross 1x.
- Costs: 4 bps aggregate target-weight turnover and 1.0% annual borrow on short gross.
- Rule-selection effect: none inside the diagnostic. Formation windows/frequencies, pair constraints,
  thresholds, timeouts, pair cap, and costs were fixed before measuring.
- Trade-selection effect: all pairs are re-formed from trailing PIT data and positions are rebuilt through
  the state machine. No ticker-PnL subtraction, full-period pair selection, or removal shortcut is used.

| monthly hold10 | `$1.089k` | `$22.463k` | `-$4.112k` | `$2.591k` | `$4.527k` | `-$4.086k` |
| quarterly hold10 | `$2.067k` | `$18.504k` | `$1.647k` | `$5.559k` | `$7.538k` | `-$0.060k` |

  target and the 2020 dependence, timeout-heavy exits, concentration, coarse SIC labels, and missing-bar

The favorable DD/Sharpe shape in 6.189 can look scalable, so I isolated the post-selection scaling effect

- QA rebuilds the 1x ending equity to within `$0.000000001` of the constituent source result.

### 6.194 Why 2022 fails and lagged SPY guard diagnostic

This diagnostic asks whether a simple, observable-before-entry market guard can contain the lead
candidate's 2022 loss. The family was frozen before this run, but it was explicitly motivated by the
already-observed 2022 failure; all results are therefore diagnostic, not clean OOS evidence.

2022 loss anatomy:

- Base candidate loses `-$47.545k` in 2022. Core contributes `-$48.661k`, pairs `+$3.393k`, financing
  `-$1.760k`, and borrow `-$0.517k`. Pairs are approximately flat after carry and do not hedge the beta
  failure.
- Core loses `-$31.735k` from the prior 15:55 mark to 09:35 and `-$16.926k` from 09:35 to 15:55. About
  65% of core loss is therefore in the overnight/opening interval and cannot be repaired by an intraday
  stop applied after 09:35.
- The first-five overlay is active on 60 sessions whose full-candidate PnL totals `-$22.126k`; the other
  190 sessions still lose `-$25.419k`. The overlay amplifies damage, but removing it cannot solve the
  underlying long-beta problem.
- Average frozen SPY exposure is 0.83x in 2022 and reaches 1.50x. Four of the five worst days have the
  extra 0.5x calendar overlay active. The five worst sessions total `-$37.779k`, although this is
  descriptive attribution rather than a valid post-hoc removal test.
- Losses are spread across January, February, April, June, August, September, and December. July and
  October rebound strongly. This bear-market/rebound alternation is why slow trend guards reduce some
  selloff exposure but also miss material recovery PnL.

Pre-registered causal guard family:

1. Keep beta but disable the 0.5x overlay when prior SPY close is below its lagged 200-session SMA.
2. Keep beta but disable the overlay when lagged SPY 20-session return is at most -8%.
3. Below the lagged SMA200, disable overlay and retain 75% of the frozen vt16 beta exposure.
4. Below the lagged SMA200, cap total frozen SPY exposure at 0.75x.

All decisions use information through the previous 15:55 mark. Pairs, their event selection, transaction
costs, financing, borrow, marks, and shared-equity compounding are unchanged. Every row is a full event
engine rebuild; no losing-day PnL is subtracted.

| variant | CAGR | PnL | dollar DD | pct DD | Sharpe | 2022 PnL | 2022 subset DD | guard days / 2022 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| baseline | 18.99% | `$223.919k` | `-$55.876k` | -22.64% | 0.881 | `-$47.545k` | `-$54.395k` | 0 / 0 |
| overlay off below SMA200 | 17.35% | `$194.974k` | `-$52.926k` | -23.25% | 0.856 | `-$42.453k` | `-$49.265k` | 377 / 211 |
| overlay off if lagged ret20 <= -8% | 17.80% | `$202.619k` | `-$59.820k` | -25.08% | 0.845 | `-$52.252k` | `-$56.652k` | 70 / 36 |
| 75% beta, overlay off below SMA200 | 16.32% | `$177.794k` | `-$45.782k` | -21.04% | 0.850 | `-$38.009k` | `-$42.762k` | 377 / 211 |
| cap total SPY at 0.75x below SMA200 | 16.82% | `$186.073k` | `-$50.852k` | -22.60% | 0.838 | `-$40.826k` | `-$47.215k` | 377 / 211 |

Provenance:

- Script: `raits/research/stocks_pit_full_lead_2022_guard_diagnostic.py`
- Inputs are the same four frozen sources as section 6.193.
- Outputs use prefix `STOCKS_PIT_FULL_LEAD_2022_GUARD_DIAGNOSTIC_2026-09-17_`: summary, yearly,
  daily, guard-state ledger, and manifest.
- Sample is touched research data from 2018-2024. No 2025-2026 data was opened.
- Rule-selection effect: none inside this five-row run; the family was fixed before execution.
- Trade-selection effect: only next-session SPY target exposure changes. Pair events remain frozen and
  all holdings, turnover, carry, and compounding are rebuilt.

Verdict:

- A lagged guard can contain part of 2022, but **none blocks it while preserving the relaxed 18% CAGR
  target**. The largest DD reduction costs 2.67 CAGR points and still leaves 2022 at `-$38.009k`.
- The 20-day crash trigger is actively harmful: it arrives during stressed conditions, misses rebounds,
  and worsens both 2022 loss and full-period DD.
- **KILL this simple lagged-guard family for the lead candidate.** Do not promote the 75%-beta row merely
  because it has the best touched-sample DD.
- The remaining credible ways to change the failure mode require a genuinely different return sleeve
  with positive 2022 convexity or a pre-funded hedge budget. Another threshold scan on SPY trend, drawdown,
  or calendar state would be optimization around the known failure and is not justified on this sample.

### 6.195 Portfolio target-gross and annual loss-budget layers

I added the two portfolio-level controls proposed after section 6.194. The family contains one fixed value
per layer rather than a threshold optimization:

- Target-gross budget: reserve 0.5x for the frozen pairs sleeve and cap the SPY target at 1.5x, for 2.0x
  intended gross. Mark-to-market movement between rebalances can temporarily exceed the target.
- Annual loss budget: if the 15:55 equity mark is at or below 90% of start-of-calendar-year equity,
  liquidate SPY and pairs at that 15:55 mark, charge turnover, remain flat through year-end, and reset at
  the next calendar year.
- Four pre-registered rows: baseline, each layer alone, and both layers together. No other cap, loss
  threshold, cooldown, or re-entry rule was tested.

| target gross 2.0x | 17.73% | `$201.473k` | `-$53.740k` | -22.64% | 0.857 | 2.03x | `-$45.727k` | 0 |
| annual loss 10% | 20.58% | `$254.296k` | `-$55.331k` | -19.58% | 1.039 | 2.59x | `-$25.138k` | 234 |

Risk behavior and attribution:

- Both breaker rows trigger exactly once, at 2022-01-26 15:55, then remain flat for 234 sessions. No

- The annual breaker halves the 2022 loss. It does not limit every peak-to-trough drawdown: the combined

### 6.196 Event-time max-drawdown circuit breakers

This test implements the max-DD family pre-registered in the user discussion immediately before the run.
All rows use the section 6.195 target-gross policy: 0.5x reserved for pairs and SPY target capped at 1.5x.

Frozen rules:

1. At -10% from the current episode's running equity peak, liquidate at 15:55 and remain flat until the
   next calendar quarter.
2. At -12.5%, liquidate at 15:55 and remain flat for 63 subsequent trading sessions.
3. At -15%, liquidate at 15:55 and remain flat until the lagged SPY close is above its lagged SMA200.

Equity is checked at both 09:35 and 15:55. A 09:35 breach is remembered, but liquidation occurs at the
same session's 15:55 executable mark, so the realized breach can exceed its threshold. SPY and pairs are
both closed, turnover is charged, and financing/borrow through liquidation remain in PnL. On re-entry the
episode high-water mark resets to current equity.

| variant | CAGR | PnL | dollar DD | pct DD | Sharpe | max gross | 2022 PnL | lock days | triggers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| gross-2 control | 17.73% | `$201.473k` | `-$53.740k` | -22.64% | 0.857 | 2.03x | `-$45.727k` | 0 | 0 |
| DD10, next quarter | 15.87% | `$170.702k` | `-$55.589k` | -21.40% | 0.766 | 2.03x | `-$46.353k` | 278 | 8 |
| DD12.5, 63 sessions | 11.36% | `$107.009k` | `-$34.580k` | -16.26% | 0.636 | 2.03x | `-$24.831k` | 384 | 6 |
| DD15, SPY SMA200 reclaim | 13.58% | `$136.442k` | `-$48.705k` | -25.28% | 0.726 | 2.03x | `-$42.321k` | 100 | 3 |

Trigger behavior:

- DD10 fires in 2018, twice in 2020, three times in 2022, 2023, and 2024. Repeated stop/re-entry episodes
  miss recoveries and make dollar DD slightly worse than the no-breaker gross-2 control.
- DD12.5 fires six times. It is the only row that materially reduces both dollar and percentage DD, but it
  remains flat for 384 sessions and sacrifices 6.37 CAGR points versus the gross-2 control.
- DD15/SMA200 fires in 2018, 2020, and 2022. Slow re-entry does not prevent the 2022 decline and produces
  the family's worst percentage DD.
- An episode DD breaker is not a hard full-history loss floor. Resetting high water after re-entry permits
  losses across multiple episodes; execution at 15:55 also permits threshold overshoot. A literal hard
  portfolio floor would require permanent shutdown after the first breach or external capital/risk reset.
